chunks.text: Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 140  Course Title: Human Relations  Prerequisites: None  Description: This course is an examination and application of basic interpersonal communication skills. Students will investigate and examine attitudes, behavior, and cultural influences that affect job and school performance. It offers structured situations in which interpersonal relationships and communication skills are explored. The course is open to students in education, the health fields, and all others who wish to explore the dynamics of getting along with people.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 250  Course Title: Small Business Management  Prerequisites: ACC 100  Description: This course presents an overview of the basic management principles, financing, accounting, and legal requirements encountered by modern small businesses. It stresses characteristics of successful business operations and incorporates the uniqueness of business enterprises on the Navajo Nation. Students will create a business plan.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 320  Course Title: Tribal Governments and Management  Prerequisites: BUS 204, MGT 360  Description: This course traces the history of tribal self-government, constitution, and the institutions in the students respective tribes and management issues faced in tribal government. The focus will be on the effectiveness, participation and issues faced by Tribal governments in achieving Tribal objectives.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 330  Course Title: Tourism and Hospitality Management  Prerequisites: ECO 201, ACC 200, MKT 240  Description: In this entryway course, students will be introduced to the major concepts, issues, and theories of tourism and hospitality as an economic sector and topic of academic study. The course will cover a broad range of topics related to the travel experience, from business development to the linkages between tourism as an industry and the impacts it has on communities and places. Students will also be introduced to key elements of the hospitality service industry and opportunities for employment within this industry.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 340  Course Title: Organizational Behavior  Prerequisites: ECO 201  Description: Provides an overview of topics and concepts in the field of Organizational Behavior. Emphasis is on developing a theoretical grasp of issues and problems and an understanding of practical implications of various theories of human behavior at work. Specific topics include leadership, motivation, teamwork, career issues, work roles, job enrichment, employee participation, and work and non-work integration.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 350  Course Title: Human Resources Management  Prerequisites: MGT 340  Description: This course examines the role of the human resource professional as a strategic partner in managing todays organizations. Key functions such as recruitment, selection, development, appraisal, retention, compensation, and labor relations are examined. Implications of legal and global environments are appraised and current issues such as diversity training, sexual harassment policies, and rising benefit costs are analyzed. Best practices of employers if choice are considered.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 360  Course Title: Principles of Management  Prerequisites: ECO 201, MKT 240  Description: This course will cover important concepts on the knowledge needed to successfully manage an organization. The course will especially be useful for those newly promoted to supervisory and managerial positions within the private, public, or federal sector.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 420  Course Title: Tribal Enterprises and Entrepreneurship  Prerequisites: ECO 201, ACC 310  Description: This course will examine different types of business enterprises existing in various tribes as the tools for economic development, including Chapter 17 Federal Corporation charter. Students will examine large scale, medium, small and micro business enterprises, tribal and private, operating within the tribal economy. Students will explore strategies to best utilize efficient use of private and tribal enterprises to promote economic development.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 425  Course Title: Management Information Systems  Prerequisites: MGT 360  Description: This is an introduction to management information systems. Topics include executive information systems, management information systems, decision support systems, expert systems, and emerging advanced systems. One-hour laboratory required.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 430  Course Title: Quality Management  Credits: 3  Prerequisites: BUS 265, MGT 360, MGT 340  Description: Prerequisite: BUS 265, MGT 340, MGT 360. This course will present the various Total Quality Management (TQM) frameworks, concepts, and quality improvement tools necessary for implementing the quality culture that characterizes world-class organizations of the 21st century. TQM is aimed at continually improving performance over the long term by focusing on customers while addressing the needs of all stakeholders. Key actions necessary for transforming business and not-for-profit organizations into world-class organizations that deliver ever-improving value to their customers, clients and constituents will be explored.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 440  Course Title: Project Management  Credits: 3  Prerequisites: MGT 360, MGT 340  Description: Prerequisite: MGT 340, MGT 360. This course develops a foundation of concepts and solutions that supports the planning, scheduling, controlling, resource allocation, and performance measurement activities required for successful completion of a project.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 450  Course Title: Strategic Management  Credits: 3  Prerequisites: MGT 360, MGT 340  Description: Prerequisite: MGT 340, MGT 360. This course deals with the development and implementation of organization strategy. It focuses on the perspectives, analytical techniques, and capabilities utilized by managers to improve an organizations probability of attaining sustainable competitive advantage and success in the long term.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MGT 460  Course Title: Tribal Leadership Challenges  Credits: 3  Prerequisites: MGT 320, MGT 420, BUS 460  Description: Prerequisite: BUS 460, MGT 320, MGT 420. This course will expose students to the traditional tribal leadership practices. Students will also study the current leadership theories and practices. The emphasis will be to help students develop their own leadership styles, philosophies and skills to be the future leaders in their respective communities.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MKT 140  Course Title: Customer Relations and Service  Credits: 3  Prerequisites: None  Description: Students will learn the techniques and guidelines for making customer service a priority. This course introduces students to the customer service environment, essential personal skills, and communication skills and challenges in the world of business.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: MKT 240  Course Title: Marketing  Credits: 3  Prerequisites: ENG 101, ECO 201, ACC 100  Description: Prerequisites: ACC 100, ECO 201. Prerequisite: ENG 101 for Fine Art Majors only. This course introduces students to basic marketing concepts and practices. Topics include the impact of external forces on marketing decisions, especially marketing on the Internet; marketing strategies; marketing aspects of business ethics and social responsibilities; and global marketing.

This course offers an in-depth look at our base 10-numeration system. It includes a study of number operations, properties of numbers and operations, computation, algorithms, and other numeration systems. Problem solving is emphasized throughout.

This course will emphasize the origin of mathematical ideas and its relation with Navajo philosophy. This course is designed as a replacement of MTH 110 or MTH 114 for non-traditional students and for students whose majors do not require higher mathematical skills and techniques.

This class focuses on Indigenous self-determination with specific attention to physical, economic, political, social and cultural resiliency factors that allow for individuals to reassess, reprioritize and reconcile the impacts of historical and contemporary trauma.

This course will examine the historical origins of the bow and arrow and its cultural-spiritual significance among Indigenous groups of North America. Students will also learn about the composition and construction of different types of bows and arrows from multiple Native American warrior societies. This requirement meets the general education requirements of Historical Awareness (HA).

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: NAS 250  Course Title: Colonization and Ethnopolitics of the Americas  Credits: 3  Prerequisites: ENG 101  Description: Prerequisite: ENG 101 or concurrent enrollment. Presents regional, hemispheric, and global laws and policies that have impacted Native American sovereignty. Focusing on concepts such as colonization, internal colonization, nationalism, and globalism, students will explore the Doctrine of Discovery, the implications of treaties, the development of encomiendas, rancherias, reservations, the creation of Federal Indian Policy; and the complexities of Native Nation Building. This class will also address how community-oriented frameworks can re-imagine current Native Nations grounded from within traditional lifeways.

NAS 305 surveys exceptions written about Navajo textiles from a range of authors including linguists, missionaries, anthropologists, traders, scholars, creative writers, and, most importantly, weavers. Topics to be investigated include material and non-material teachings such as techniques, taboos, storytelling, and value. In addition to reading about Navajo textile creations, students will be required to finish a weaving throughout the class, exploring the sensorial process and metacognitive relationships that Navajo people have with textile productions.

Department: Course Descriptions  Course Code: NAS 316  Course Title: Indigenous Relationships with the More-than-Human  Credits: 3  Prerequisites: None  Description: This course deconstructs anthropocentrism (human-centered perspective) to understand how Indigenous relationships between human and non-human animals are created, maintained, and destroyed.
